title: That’s Not the Feedback I Need! - Student Engagement with GenAI Feedback in the Tutor Kai
venue: Proceedings of 2025 Conference on United Kingdom & Ireland Computing Education Research (UKICER ’25)
extended_summary:
This paper examines how undergraduate computing students engage with generative AI feedback while solving introductory Python programming tasks, and whether that feedback actually helps their problem-solving. The authors note that prior work has largely focused on evaluating the quality of AI-generated feedback itself, rather than how students attend to, interpret, and use that feedback during learning. The study asks two main questions: how much attention students pay to GenAI feedback compared with compiler feedback, and to what extent GenAI feedback is helpful, especially for students with and without prior programming experience.

To investigate this, the authors used a custom web application called Tutor Kai that presented Python tasks, a code editor, compiler feedback, and GenAI feedback generated by OpenAI’s GPT-4-turbo model. Students could run code, view compiler output and test results, and then request GenAI feedback. The study combined multiple methods: eye-tracking to measure visual attention across interface regions, think-aloud protocols during problem-solving, and semi-structured interviews afterward. Helpfulness was judged by triangulating whether students read the feedback, verbalized understanding, and made code changes aligned with the feedback.

The study involved 11 undergraduate computer science students at a German university, drawn from an Object-Oriented and Functional Programming course. Participants were mostly first- and second-semester students and were split into inexperienced and experienced programmers based on prior self-reported programming background. The study took place in a controlled laboratory setting during individual two-hour sessions. Students worked on six Python tasks developed for the course context, while their interactions, gaze behavior, and reflections were recorded.

The main findings show that GenAI feedback attracted substantial attention and was generally viewed positively by students, but its usefulness differed by experience level. Inexperienced students spent about twice as much fixation time on GenAI feedback as experienced students, requested it more frequently, and often ignored compiler feedback. Experienced students used GenAI feedback more effectively: a higher proportion of the feedback advanced their problem-solving, and they were better able to interpret and act on it. For inexperienced students, GenAI feedback was often too vague, used unfamiliar technical vocabulary, lacked syntax-level guidance, or was insufficiently precise. The authors conclude that GenAI feedback has promise in programming education, but its benefits depend strongly on learner prior knowledge and should be adapted to students’ experience and informational needs.

identified_tools.name: Tutor Kai
identified_tools.description: A custom web application for programming education that provides Python tasks, a code editor, compiler feedback, and GenAI-generated feedback to students.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied as the interface through which 11 undergraduate students solved Python programming tasks while requesting and engaging with GenAI feedback and compiler feedback; the paper examined visual attention, perceived helpfulness, and problem-solving support.

findings.finding_summary: In a mixed-methods lab study with 11 undergraduate students, Tutor Kai's GenAI feedback received 23.79% of total fixation time, compared with 7.00% for compiler feedback and 15.29% for the task description. Inexperienced students spent 30.71% of fixation time on GenAI feedback versus 15.49% for experienced students, while experienced students spent 9.35% on compiler feedback versus 5.05% for inexperienced students.
findings.measure: Eye-tracking fixation time across interface Areas of Interest (GenAI feedback, compiler feedback, task description, code editor)

findings.finding_summary: Across 171 GenAI feedback outputs in Tutor Kai, 49.7% were coded as helping students advance problem-solving, whereas only 17.4% of 287 compiler feedback messages were coded as helpful. Helpfulness differed by prior experience: GenAI feedback helped in 60.9% of cases for experienced students and 43.0% for inexperienced students; experienced students also requested 28% less GenAI feedback overall (64 vs. 107 requests).
findings.measure: Observed helpfulness of GenAI and compiler feedback during programming problem-solving, based on triangulated eye-tracking and think-aloud coding
findings.sample_size: n=11; 171 GenAI feedback outputs; 287 compiler feedback messages

findings.finding_summary: Tutor Kai's GenAI feedback was less comprehensible for inexperienced students: 20.6% of GenAI feedback cases for inexperienced students (22 out of 107) were not comprehended, compared with 1.6% for experienced students (1 out of 64). Among 77 instances where GenAI feedback was coded as not helpful, reasons included incomprehensible feedback (23 cases), missing needed Python syntax despite semantic understanding (17 cases), and insufficiently precise error localization (13 cases).
findings.measure: Comprehensibility and failure modes of GenAI feedback during task solving
findings.sample_size: n=11; 107 inexperienced-student GenAI cases; 64 experienced-student GenAI cases; 77 not-helpful instances

findings.finding_summary: In post-task interviews, students rated the helpfulness of Tutor Kai's GenAI feedback at an average of 8.59 on a 10-point Likert scale, and all 11 students stated that the GenAI feedback increased their motivation to solve programming tasks. However, this positive perception contrasted with the more mixed observed helpfulness during problem-solving.
findings.measure: Interview-based helpfulness rating and self-reported motivation

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's GPT-family large language model, normalized here from the model used to generate feedback.
identified_tools.use_case: Used under the hood in Tutor Kai to generate programming feedback via OpenAI's gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 model for Python tasks.

findings.finding_summary: Using ChatGPT-generated feedback within Tutor Kai, 49.7% of 171 feedback outputs were coded as helping students advance problem-solving. The benefit was higher for experienced students (60.9%) than inexperienced students (43.0%), and inexperienced students did not comprehend 20.6% of the feedback they received (22/107) versus 1.6% for experienced students (1/64).
findings.measure: Helpfulness and comprehensibility of ChatGPT-generated programming feedback

quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical mixed-methods study using eye-tracking, think-aloud protocols, and interviews, but it is qualitative/exploratory with a small sample (n=11) and no randomized or quasi-experimental design.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports promising but mixed outcomes: GenAI feedback was often helpful and motivating, yet benefits varied strongly by prior experience and no standardized effect sizes were reported.
